search_log: Searched “Basket Case” “Carl Hiaasen” with excerpt, first chapter, point of view, first person, narrator, and narrated-by terms.
Opened the Publishers Weekly author interview, the Daily Nexus contemporary review, an interior Whichbook extract, Google Books, Penguin Random House, and Carl Hiaasen's official book page.
Targeted searches for alternating narration, multiple narrators, epistolary form, frame narrative, and third-person sections found no credible contrary structure.
Bookreporter's chapter-one excerpt timed out when opened, and the official-site Amazon preview returned an internal error; neither inaccessible preview was used as evidence.
Google Books and the publisher/author pages verified the work but did not themselves explicitly establish narrative person.
person_note: The diagnostic event passages q00006 and q00008 expose Jack Tagger as a participating first-person narrator. Third-person references to other characters in q00007 and q00011 are unmarked rather than evidence of third-person narration; dialogue and gnomic passages are local or nondiagnostic. Hiaasen's whole-book account of his narrative choice, an independent contemporary review, and an interior extract all agree that the novel remains in Jack's first-person perspective. No credible evidence of sustained narration in another person was found; the only minor uncertainty is that the accessible extracts do not reproduce every section of the book.
